summary: C++ tutorial building APawnWithCamera: a Pawn with a USpringArmComponent and UCameraComponent, mouse pitch/yaw, WASD movement and a right-mouse zoom that lerps FieldOfView and TargetArmLength in Tick. Full header and .cpp listings included.
gotchas: Uses legacy Action/Axis Mappings under Project Settings > Engine > Input > Bindings, not Enhanced Input
Listings mix variable names (OurCameraSpringArm vs SpringArmComp) and show a mistyped include "Camera/Component.h"; the finished .cpp uses Camera/CameraComponent.h
Camera pitch is clamped between -80 and -15 degrees so it always looks down

summary: C++ tutorial making a Countdown actor with a UTextRenderComponent driven by a repeating timer (SetTimer/ClearTimer with an FTimerHandle), exposing the time via UPROPERTY(EditAnywhere) and the finish event as a BlueprintNativeEvent overridden in a Blueprint child. Explains BlueprintCallable vs BlueprintImplementableEvent vs BlueprintNativeEvent and Add call to parent function.
gotchas: Editor-set property values are applied after the constructor but before BeginPlay, so read them in BeginPlay
A BlueprintNativeEvent's C++ body must be in a virtual function named <Name>_Implementation
Overriding the event in Blueprint replaces the C++ behaviour unless you add a call to the parent function

summary: C++ tutorial building ACollidingPawn with a USphereComponent root, visual static mesh, toggleable particle system, spring-arm camera, and a custom UPawnMovementComponent whose TickComponent uses ConsumeInputVector, SafeMoveUpdatedComponent and SlideAlongSurface to collide and slide. Shows overriding GetMovementComponent and binding input.
gotchas: Movement components are not Scene Components, so they are not attached; set UpdatedComponent instead
The .generated.h include must be the last include in the header or compile errors occur
Hard-coded asset paths via ConstructorHelpers are not best practice; the page prefers setting assets in a Blueprint
Uses legacy Action/Axis Mappings and a Cascade particle system (P_Fire); custom movement has no gravity

summary: Explains running GenerateProjectFiles.bat (a wrapper around UnrealBuildTool -ProjectFiles) to create UE5.sln and IDE project files for source builds, with its command-line options and notes on source control and the UnrealVS refresh button.
gotchas: Written for engines built from GitHub source
Re-run after syncing code or adding/removing source files; do not hand-edit project files
Project files are intermediates and should not be checked into source control

summary: Overview of UE modules: folder layout with Public/Private, [ModuleName].Build.cs with Public/PrivateDependencyModuleNames, IMPLEMENT_MODULE with FDefaultModuleImpl, and the .uproject/.uplugin Modules list (Type, LoadingPhase, platform/target include/exclude lists).
gotchas: Unreal modules are unrelated to C++20 modules
UBT builds from Target.cs/Build.cs and ignores the IDE solution; regenerate project files after editing Build.cs or moving files
Load order of modules within the same LoadingPhase is not deterministic; use LoadModule/LoadModuleChecked
Plugin classes not found by the editor can be fixed by setting LoadingPhase to PreDefault

summary: Material Editor organization tools: node comment bubbles, comment boxes (C key), reroute nodes, Named Reroutes (declaration/usage nodes), align and distribute shortcuts, and Collapse Nodes/Expand Node.
gotchas: Give each Named Reroute Declaration a unique descriptive name in the Details panel

summary: How to add Material Expressions and Functions to a graph via the Palette, right-click menu, dragging from pins, hotkey+click shortcuts (1-4, M, L, S, U, etc.), and dragging Material Functions from the Content Browser; also connecting and deleting wires.
keys: Edit > Editor Preferences > Keyboard Shortcuts > Material Editor Spawn Nodes
gotchas: Engine Material Functions are hidden until Show Engine Content is enabled in the Content Browser
Alt+click a wire deletes it; Ctrl+click drags it to another pin

summary: Previewing materials in the Material Editor viewport (Realtime, preview meshes, custom mesh, Preview Scene Settings, Start Previewing Node), compiling with Apply/Save, applying materials by drag-drop or the Details panel, and live-tweaking Scalar/Vector parameters in the level.
keys: Use Selected Asset from Content Browser
gotchas: A material must be compiled with Apply or Save before it shows changes in the level
Live in-level previewing only works with Scalar/Vector parameters, not Constant nodes

summary: Explains the Main Material Node: inputs and their defaults (Metallic 0, Specular 0.5, Roughness 0.5), how Material Domain, Blend Mode and Shading Model enable/disable inputs, and a summary of each Details panel section.
gotchas: Nodes wired to disabled inputs stay connected but are ignored when compiling
Translucency settings are only editable when Blend Mode is Translucent; Post Process settings only when Domain is Post Process

summary: Step-by-step creation of a separate runtime C++ module (ModuleTest): folders, Build.cs, IMPLEMENT_MODULE, registering in the .uproject Modules list, adding it to the primary module's dependencies, compiling only that module with Build.bat, and adding classes to it via the New Class Wizard.
gotchas: Regenerate project files after adding a module, changing Build.cs, or moving/renaming files
Major changes or new classes may need the editor closed and restarted after compiling
Class only shows as a Blueprint parent if its header is in Public, it is BlueprintType, and the module is a dependency

summary: Overview of the Collab Viewer Templates (OEM/Manufacturing and AEC) for multi-user VR and desktop design reviews, with the package-and-host-server workflow and OpenXR VR support.

Virtual production guide for driving a VCam Actor from the Unreal VCam iOS/Android app over Live Link and Pixel Streaming: required plugins, device requirements, connecting, input profiles, and the app's camera controls and logs.
gotchas: Virtual Camera does not support Pixel Streaming 2
Requires iOS/iPadOS 15+ with ARKit or Android 24+ with ARCore

summary: Hub page for XR: links to OpenXR head-mounted development, handheld AR, getting started, XR input, XR UI, shared experiences, supported devices, XR profiling, and XR content-creation tools (Virtual Scouting, LiveLinkXR, Live Link VRPN, iOS face capture).
gotchas: OpenXR in Unreal Engine currently only supports head-mounted devices

summary: Quickstart for the Handheld AR template on ARKit/ARCore phones: user journey, Android and iOS packaging setup, touch gestures for placing/scaling/rotating objects, UI menus, and the key Blueprint assets.
gotchas: Device must support ARKit (iOS) or ARCore (Android)
Snapshots save to the camera roll on Android but not on iOS (as of 4.27)

summary: Technical reference for the Handheld AR template's Blueprints: BP_ARPawn state machine, light estimation, plane candidate creation, gesture recognition, BP_Placeable, BP_Plane materials, and the BP_StylizedUI/DT_Styles UI styling system.
Describes the In-Camera VFX template for LED stage virtual production: nDisplay config, inner/outer frustum, Live Link, chroma key, color correction regions, and the LED_CurvedStage map.
gotchas: Template assets need Show Engine Content and Show Plugin Content enabled in the Content Browser

summary: Creating a project from the nDisplay template and the example multi-display configurations it ships with in ExampleConfigs.
Customizing the Product Configurator template: building Variant Sets in a LevelVariantSet with the Variant Manager and connecting it to BP_Configurator, which generates a runtime UMG option UI.
gotchas: The first and second Variant Sets must be Environment and Camera for the generated UI to work
The LevelVariantSet Actor must be placed in the level for BP_Configurator to see it

summary: Overview of the VR Virtual Scouting tools for filmmakers, built on the XR Creative Framework, with supported headsets and a link to setup.
gotchas: Requires UE 5.4+, Windows VR-capable PC and Quest 2/3/Pro, Rift S or Valve Index
Virtual Scouting Legacy tools and unused VREditor code will be deprecated in a future release

summary: Guide to the OpenXR-based VR Template: VRPawn/VRGameMode, teleport and snap-turn locomotion limited by NavModifierVolume, GrabComponent grab types, UMG menu, and the VR Spectator controls.
gotchas: VR Spectator is not compatible with mobile VR devices such as Quest
Template input uses legacy Action and Axis Mappings

summary: Very short overview: AIController controls a Pawn by observing the world and making decisions without human input, in contrast to PlayerController.
Defines Blueprint Classes, the common parent classes (Actor, Pawn, Character, PlayerController, Game Mode), Blueprint inheritance from other Blueprints, and Data-Only Blueprints.
gotchas: Data-Only Blueprints can only tweak inherited properties; adding code, variables or components converts them to full Blueprints

summary: Overview of the Character class: a Pawn with CharacterMovementComponent, CapsuleComponent and SkeletalMeshComponent for walking, jumping, flying, swimming, and what CharacterMovementComponent configures.
gotchas: CharacterMovementComponent assumes a vertically oriented capsule for collision
CharacterMovementComponent is specific to Characters and cannot be used by other classes

summary: Using the Blueprint Editor Components window: adding, removing, transforming and renaming components, assigning assets (e.g. Static Mesh) to them, and creating component events such as overlap events via Add Event.
gotchas: Transforming a parent component propagates to all children
Shift-snapping in the viewport requires Level Editor snapping to be enabled

summary: Quick reference table for core gameplay classes: Pawn, Character, Controller, PlayerController, AIController, HUD, PlayerCameraManager, GameMode, GameState, PlayerState, and how they relate.
gotchas: GameMode exists only on the server; GameState and PlayerState replicate to clients

summary: Using BSP Geometry Brushes for level blockout: placing primitives from Place Actors > Geometry, additive vs subtractive types, solidity, brush order, surface properties, Brush Editing Mode, and converting with Create Static Mesh.
gotchas: Not recommended for final level geometry; use Static Meshes or Modeling Mode
Keep brush vertices on the drag grid to avoid rendering artifacts
Brush order matters: subtractive placed before additive is ignored
Brushes must be converted with Create Static Mesh to use Modeling Mode tools

summary: Hub/overview of Levels: a Level is a .umap file holding environment actors, player character, lights and sounds; links to Static and Skeletal Mesh Actor pages.

Overview of the Pawn base class, one-to-one Controller possession, moving Pawns with SetActorLocation (teleport or sweep), and the DefaultPawn and SpectatorPawn subclasses with their flying movement components.
gotchas: Pawns spawned during gameplay are not automatically possessed by a Controller

summary: Short overview of PlayerController as the human player's interface to a Pawn, and when to put input handling and persistent data (e.g. score) in the PlayerController instead of the Pawn.
gotchas: The Pawn can be destroyed and respawned while the PlayerController persists, so data kept on the Pawn resets

summary: Overview of the Project Settings window (Edit > Project Settings): searchable categories, import/export, and how settings map to Config/DefaultEngine.ini versus platform ini files.
gotchas: Platform-specific .ini files must be edited manually in a text editor

summary: High-level workflow for a playable animated character: import Skeletal Mesh, make a PlayerController, a Character Blueprint for movement, an Animation Blueprint assigned via Anim Blueprint Generated Class, and a GameMode set through World Settings GameMode Override.
gotchas: At minimum set Default Pawn Class and Player Controller Class in the GameMode to test a character

summary: Describes the simplified Blueprint Editor UI for Blueprint Interface assets (function signatures only) and why its graph view is read-only.
gotchas: Blueprint Interfaces cannot add variables, edit graphs, or add components

summary: Describes the Level Blueprint (per-level global event graph for level events, level streaming, Sequencer and placed-actor bindings) and which Blueprint Editor panels it shows.
gotchas: Each level has one Level Blueprint; new Level Blueprints cannot be created through the editor

summary: Describes Blueprint Macro Library assets (shared reusable macro graphs expanded at compile time) and the Blueprint Editor panels shown when editing one.
gotchas: Macro changes only appear in graphs that use them after those Blueprints are recompiled

summary: Reference for the Physics Asset Editor Tools tab (body creation settings like Primitive Type, Min Bone Size, constraint creation, regenerate bodies) and Profiles tab (Physical Animation and Constraint profiles, assign/unassign).
gotchas: Tapered Capsule primitive type is for cloth only
Position and Velocity Strength are only used for non-local simulation

summary: Tour of the Physics Asset Editor UI for Skeletal Mesh ragdolls: toolbar (simulation, collision toggles), Skeleton Tree, Constraints Graph, Viewport, Details/Preview Scene Settings, and Tools/Profiles panels.
gotchas: Tools panel settings are also the defaults used when importing a Skeletal Mesh with Create Physics Asset enabled
